name: Iris purple
lede: Iris purple is a vivid, reddish purple named for the iris flower, whose petals range far wider than any one swatch could show.

sections.title: A flower with many purples
sections.body:
The name comes from [[iris]], a genus of several hundred species whose flowers run from near-white through yellow to the deep violets and purples the genus is best known for [1]. Our color library does not carry an entry for this exact xkcd-survey shade, so it has no recorded first-use date or dictionary pedigree beyond the 2010 crowd survey that coined it [1].

Against our own data, Iris purple sits at lightness 43 and a high chroma of 86, closer to magenta-red than to the blue-violet most people picture when they hear "iris" [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[purple-munsell]], [[purply]] and [[dark-orchid]], at 4.3, 4.5 and 5.3 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, has no painting where this saturated purple covers five percent or more of the canvas [2]. Pigments able to reach this chroma at this darkness are a modern, synthetic achievement; historical purples came from madder, cochineal, or orchil, and none hold this hue at this strength once varnished and aged [2]. The absence is a property of the pigments available to painters, not of the flower.
